classification: Acceptance coverage for the inspected/reproduced atomic provisioning defect; the cross-process lock and private atomic replacement were already implemented. No new demonstrated production defect was found in these interruption checks.
executed_validation: Ten real SIGKILL cases: new keys and legacy 32-byte signing seed at creation, completed write, file fsync, rename and parent-directory fsync barriers.

For each case eight independent fresh processes are held behind the actual initialization lock until all eight opened its descriptor; then all converge on signing identity and SHA-256 fingerprint of the transport private key. A separate fresh process reopens the same identity.

Assertions require all interrupted material private before kill, no partial published key, legacy signing seed unchanged, and already-renamed 64-byte identity preserved byte-for-byte. All retained children have bounded deadlines and owner cleanup; only synthetic marked temporary roots are touched.

cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked --all-targets: 264 passed, zero failed, five original opt-in ignores unchanged; cargo build --release --locked --bin mywhisper.
compatibility: No key format, signing identity, transport identity, database, settings or protocol change. Test-only thread-local barriers are absent from production binaries; the production replacement sequence is unchanged.
limitations: SIGKILL interruption does not establish physical power-loss durability or every filesystem/permission failure path.
Private orphan staging files are not adopted or claimed as published identities. Automatic orphan sweeping is not added; disposable roots clean up after all children are reaped.

Latest fresh Nix/native/live acceptance remains the ce6b000 production checkpoint with 263 tests, preserved separately. This checkpoint adds test-only fault barriers and one regression; the complete final candidate must rerun all required gates.
Full original shutdown, storage, sync, provider and release-acceptance obligations remain open; no PR submitted.
